units.CD4305-businga: Businga territory (Nord-Ubangi) lies in the interior of north-western DRC, south of Gbadolite, between the Ubangi border and the Mongala river basin, far from the eastern conflict zones. It comprises the Businga town (territorial seat on the Gbadolite–Gemena/Lisala road), the Karawa area (a large mission/market agglomeration) and the Loko area, plus rural villages. No Congolese or foreign armed group is known to hold or tax territory here; the state (PNC in towns and villages, territorial administration, ANR and occasional FARDC elements, plus customary chiefs) is the de facto authority. Insecurity is limited to ordinary crime, inter-communal or land disputes and occasional abuses by state agents, which do not amount to territorial control. No web research was possible in this run (web search budget exhausted and Wikipedia blocked by the egress proxy), so this rests on default state presence and general background knowledge.
